newsitem.title: CANADA: Busang still in flux despite Jakarta statement.
newsitem.headline: Busang still in flux despite Jakarta statement.

text.p: The rights to the huge Busang gold deposit still appear to be in flux, despite a statement from the Indonesian government on Monday saying Barrick Gold Corp and Bre-X Minerals Ltd agreed to a government proposal to split the spectacular Busang gold find.

"Nothing to my knowledge has changed," Bre-X spokesman Steve McAnulty said in a phone interview from Calgary. "We still don't have a deal. There are a number of points that are still being negotiated."
"I can explain to you that we don't have a signed agreement," Barrick spokesman Vince Borg said in an interview.
The Indonesian government told Reuters in Jakarta on Monday that the two companies agreed to split the deposit, with Barrick getting 75 percent and Bre-X keeping 25 percent.
"They have reported they can both accept the government suggestion" of a 25-75 split, said Umar Said, secretary-general of the Mines Ministry.
"They are also ready to provide a 10 percent stake to the government. It is good," he said.
But Bre-X said the whole deal was still up in the air.
"We are negotiating toward an end," McAnulty said.
He said legal issues stood in the way of an agreement.
McAnulty said Bre-X still hoped the Indonesian government would open up the negotiation process for Busang to allow other companies to bid.

"We're getting signals from the consulate, from the embassy, from Mr. Said," he said. "We certainly hope the government allows the process to proceed as originally planned. It would be to the best interest of Bre-X shareholders."
Vancouver-based gold firm Placer Dome Inc has complained about being shut out of the process despite months of negotiations.
The companies are wrangling over the Busang gold discovery on the island of Borneo. The deposit contains at least 57 million ounces ot gold, which could be mined at low cost.

The government set a December 4 deadline for the two companies to work out an agreement. Bre-X and Barrick reported on December 4 that they had agreed on some points but that no final deal had been signed.
"When we come to acceptable terms, we'll announce it," said Barrick's Borg. "We're back to where we were last week."

Neither company would provide details about the terms of a deal, when the terms would be announced, whether shareholders would be able to vote on the agreement or who would be granted essential permits giving the companies rights to the deposit.
